S.h: Something heavy came with you today.
S.p: You don’t have to explain it or hurry it along. Many people in Scripture carried something heavy too.

F.h: Worry for the people you love back home can follow you everywhere.
F.p: Family, friends, news of conflict, or no news at all can keep your mind from resting. Someone in Scripture heard hard news about his people and brought it straight to God.

A.p: It’s all right that it stirs you up. Scripture has room for people who cried out to God before their words were tidy.

J.h: Something good is close, even if it feels fragile.
J.p: Good things belong in prayer too. You can bring this to God just as it is.

SF.h: You may be worn out, and afraid of what comes next.
SF.p: Someone in Scripture ran until he had nothing left. God met him there, gently.

SA.h: Loss can come with a question: why did this have to happen?
SA.p: You can bring the loss and the question to God together. You don’t have to choose the polite one.

SJ.h: Something good and something painful are here at the same time.
SJ.p: You don’t have to choose one. Both can be true, and both can be brought to God.

FA.h: You may have been treated unfairly, and now you’re not sure you’re safe.
FA.p: Someone in Scripture ran from people who hurt her. In the wilderness, God saw her and called her by name.

FJ.h: Something good happened, and part of you is afraid it won’t last.
FJ.p: You can thank God and still tell Him what scares you. Someone in Scripture, after years of distress, called God her rock.

AJ.h: Something good is here, and something that hurt you is still real.
AJ.p: Being thankful doesn’t mean the wrong didn’t matter. God can hold both, so you don’t have to hold them alone.

NW.h: You don’t have to find words right now.
NW.p: Someone in Scripture was too troubled to speak, and prayed anyway. You can let his words speak for you.
